summary: Someone who kills a person by accident must go into galus, to a city of refuge. This mishnah teaches the rule: if it happened while something was moving downward, he goes into galus; if not, he does not.

chunks.en: These are the people who go into galus:
chunks.explain: Galus means going to live in a city of refuge.
chunks.st: These are the people who are exiled:

chunks.en: someone who kills a person by accident.
chunks.st: Anyone who kills a person unintentionally.
chunks.stMore: Whether one is liable to be exiled depends on the particular circumstances of the case:

chunks.he: הָיָה מְעַגֵּל בְּמַעְגִּילָה וְנָפְלָה עָלָיו וַהֲרָגַתּוּ,
chunks.en: If he was rolling a roller on his roof, and it fell on someone and killed him,
chunks.explain: A heavy roller was used to smooth a roof.
chunks.st: If one was rolling a roller to smooth the covering of mortar that he applied to seal his roof and the roller fell upon a person and killed him,

chunks.he: הָיָה מְשַׁלְשֵׁל בְּחָבִית וְנָפְלָה עָלָיו וַהֲרָגַתּוּ,
chunks.en: or he was lowering a barrel, and it fell on someone and killed him,
chunks.st: or if one was lowering a barrel from the roof and it fell on a person and killed him,

chunks.he: הָיָה יוֹרֵד בְּסֻלָּם וְנָפַל עָלָיו וַהֲרָגוֹ,
chunks.en: or he was going down a ladder, and he fell on someone and killed him,
chunks.st: or if he was descending a ladder and he fell on a person and killed him,

chunks.en: he goes into galus.
chunks.st: in all of these cases, he is exiled.

chunks.en: But if he was pulling a roller toward himself,
chunks.st: But if one was pulling a roller toward him

chunks.en: and it fell on someone and killed him,
chunks.st: and it fell from his hands upon a person and killed him,

chunks.en: or he was pulling up a barrel,
chunks.st: or if one was lifting a barrel

chunks.en: and the rope tore and it fell on someone and killed him,
chunks.st: and the rope was severed and it fell upon a person and killed him,

chunks.he: הָיָה עוֹלֶה בְסֻלָּם וְנָפַל עָלָיו וַהֲרָגוֹ,
chunks.en: or he was climbing up a ladder, and he fell on someone and killed him,
chunks.st: or if one was climbing a ladder and he fell upon a person and killed him,

chunks.en: he does not go into galus.
chunks.st: that unintentional murderer is not exiled.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: Whenever it happened while moving downward,
chunks.st: Any murderer who kills unintentionally through his downward

chunks.en: he goes into galus.
chunks.st: motion is exiled,

chunks.en: And when it was not while moving downward,
chunks.st: and one who kills not through his downward

chunks.en: he does not go into galus.
chunks.st: motion is not exiled.

chunks.en: If the iron head of an ax slipped off its handle and killed someone,
chunks.st: If the blade of an ax or hatchet was displaced from its handle, and it flew through the air and killed a person,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:

chunks.en: he does not go into galus.
chunks.st: He is not exiled,

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: and the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he goes into galus.
chunks.st: He is exiled.

chunks.en: If a piece of wood flew off a log being chopped and killed someone,
chunks.st: If part of a tree that is being split flew through the air and killed a person,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:

chunks.en: he goes into galus.
chunks.st: The murderer is exiled,

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: and the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he does not go into galus.
chunks.st: He is not exiled.

summary: Someone who throws a stone and kills by accident goes into galus only if the person was allowed to be in that place. Abba Shaul adds that someone doing a mitzvah, like a father teaching his son, does not go into galus.

chunks.en: Someone who threw a stone into a public place and killed someone
chunks.st: One who threw a stone into the public domain and killed

chunks.en: goes into galus.
chunks.st: a person is exiled.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says:

chunks.en: If after the stone left his hand,
chunks.st: If after the stone left his hand

chunks.en: the other person stuck out his head and got hit,
chunks.st: the other person placed his head out into the public domain and received a blow from the stone,

chunks.en: he is free.
chunks.explain: When he threw it, nobody was there.
chunks.st: he is exempt,
chunks.stMore: as when he cast the stone into the public domain there was no one there.

chunks.en: If he threw a stone into his own courtyard and killed someone,
chunks.st: In the case of one who threw the stone into his courtyard and killed a person,

chunks.he: אִם יֵשׁ רְשׁוּת לַנִּזָּק לִכָּנֵס לְשָׁם,
chunks.en: if the person who got hurt was allowed to go in there,
chunks.st: if the victim had permission to enter into there,

chunks.en: he goes into galus.
chunks.st: the murderer is exiled,

chunks.en: But if not,
chunks.st: but if not,

chunks.en: he does not go into galus,
chunks.st: he is not exiled,

chunks.en: as it says, "And someone who goes
chunks.st: as it is stated with regard to the cities of refuge: “And as one

chunks.en: with his friend into the forest."
chunks.st: who goes with his neighbor into the forest” (Deuteronomy 19:5),
chunks.stMore: from which it is derived:

chunks.en: Just as the forest is a place where the one who gets hurt
chunks.st: Just as with regard to a forest, the victim

chunks.en: and the one who hurts are both allowed to go in,
chunks.st: and the assailant both have equal permission to enter there,
chunks.stMore: so too, with regard to all places that the victim and the assailant have permission to enter there, the killer is liable.

chunks.en: this leaves out a homeowner's courtyard,
chunks.st: This serves to exclude the courtyard of the homeowner,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין רְשׁוּת לַנִּזָּק וְלַמַּזִּיק לִכָּנֵס לְשָׁם.
chunks.en: where the one who gets hurt and the one who hurts are not both allowed to go in.
chunks.st: where the victim and the assailant do not both have permission to enter there.
chunks.stMore: Since the victim had no right to enter his courtyard, the unintentional murderer is exempt from exile.

chunks.en: Abba Shaul says,
chunks.st: Abba Shaul says:
chunks.stMore: Another halakha can be derived from that verse:

chunks.en: Just as chopping wood is something a person chooses to do,
chunks.explain: Galus is only when he did not have to be doing it.
chunks.st: Just as the cutting of wood that is mentioned in the verse is optional,
chunks.stMore: so too, all those liable to be exiled are examples of cases where the unintentional murderer was engaged in an activity that is optional.

chunks.en: this leaves out a father who hits his son to teach him,
chunks.st: This serves to exclude a father who strikes his son,

chunks.en: and a teacher who hits his student,
chunks.st: and a teacher who oppresses his student,

chunks.en: and the messenger of Beis Din who gives lashes.
chunks.st: and an agent of the court deputized to flog transgressors.
chunks.stMore: If, in the course of performing the mitzva with which they are charged, they unintentionally murdered the son, the student, or the person being flogged, respectively, they are exempt.

summary: This mishnah teaches who goes into galus for killing whom by accident. Someone who hated the person he killed usually does not go into galus, because it may not have been an accident.

chunks.en: A father goes into galus because of his son,
chunks.st: The father is exiled to a city of refuge due to his unintentional murder of his son.

chunks.en: and a son goes into galus because of his father.
chunks.st: And the son is exiled due to his unintentional murder of his father.

chunks.en: Everyone goes into galus because of a Jew,
chunks.st: Everyone is exiled due to their unintentional murder of a Jew,

chunks.en: and a Jew goes into galus because of any of them,
chunks.st: and a Jew is exiled due to his unintentional murder of any of them,

chunks.en: except because of a ger toshav.
chunks.explain: A non-Jew living in Eretz Yisrael who keeps the seven mitzvos of Noach.
chunks.st: except for the unintentional murder of a gentile who resides in Eretz Yisrael and observes the seven Noahide mitzvot [ger toshav].

chunks.en: And a ger toshav goes into galus only
chunks.st: And a ger toshav is exiled only

chunks.en: because of a ger toshav.
chunks.st: due to his unintentional murder of a ger toshav.

chunks.en: A blind person does not go into galus.
chunks.st: A blind person who unintentionally murdered another is not exiled;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: he goes into galus.
chunks.st: He is exiled.

chunks.en: Someone who hated the person does not go into galus.
chunks.st: The enemy of the victim is not exiled,
chunks.stMore: as presumably it was not a completely unintentional act.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: The one who hated him is put to death,
chunks.st: Not only is an enemy not exiled, but he is executed by the court,

chunks.en: because he is like someone who was warned.
chunks.explain: He probably did it on purpose.
chunks.st: because his halakhic status is like that of one who is forewarned by witnesses
chunks.stMore: not to perform the action, as presumably he performed the action intentionally.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: There is an enemy who goes into galus,
chunks.st: There is an enemy who is exiled

chunks.en: and there is an enemy who does not go into galus.
chunks.st: and there is an enemy who is not exiled.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁהוּא יָכוֹל לוֹמַר לְדַעַת הָרַג,
chunks.en: Whenever one could say he killed on purpose,
chunks.st: In any case where an observer could say he killed knowingly,
chunks.stMore: where circumstances lead to the assumption that it was an intentional act,

chunks.en: he does not go into galus.
chunks.st: the enemy is not exiled,
chunks.stMore: even if he claims that he acted unintentionally.

chunks.en: But if he clearly killed without meaning to,
chunks.st: And if it is clear that he killed unknowingly,
chunks.stMore: as circumstances indicate that he acted unintentionally,

chunks.en: he goes into galus.
chunks.st: he is exiled, even though the victim is his enemy.

summary: Someone who killed by accident goes to one of the six cities of refuge: three across the Yarden and three in Eretz Yisrael. The cities only started working once all six were chosen.

chunks.en: Where do they go into galus?
chunks.st: To where are the unintentional murderers exiled?

chunks.en: To the cities of refuge:
chunks.explain: Special cities where he is safe from the relatives of the one he killed.
chunks.st: They are exiled to cities of refuge,

chunks.he: לַשָּׁלשׁ שֶׁבְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן וְלַשָּׁלשׁ שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן,
chunks.en: to the three across the Yarden and the three in the land of Canaan,
chunks.st: to three cities that were in the east bank of the Jordan and to three cities that were in the land of Canaan,
chunks.stMore: i.e., Eretz Yisrael,

words.en: that are in the land of

chunks.en: as it says, "Three cities
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Three cities

chunks.he: תִּתְּנוּ מֵעֵבֶר לַיַּרְדֵּן וְאֵת שְׁלשׁ הֶעָרִים
chunks.en: you shall give across the Yarden, and three cities
chunks.st: shall you give beyond the Jordan and three cities

chunks.en: you shall give in the land of Canaan."
chunks.st: shall you give in the land of Canaan; they shall be cities of refuge” (Numbers 35:14).
chunks.stMore: The mishna comments:

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְחֲרוּ שָׁלשׁ שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: Until the three in Eretz Yisrael were chosen,
chunks.st: Until the three cities of refuge that were in Eretz Yisrael were selected,

words.en: that are in the land of

chunks.he: לֹא הָיוּ שָׁלשׁ שֶׁבְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן קוֹלְטוֹת,
chunks.en: the three across the Yarden did not take anyone in,
chunks.st: an unintentional murderer would not be admitted to the three that were in the east bank of the Jordan,
chunks.stMore: even though the latter three were already selected by Moses (see Deuteronomy 4:41),

chunks.en: as it says, "Six cities of refuge shall there be,"
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Six cities of refuge shall they be” (Numbers 35:13),

chunks.en: so they work only when all six take people in together.
chunks.st: from which it is derived that they do not become cities of refuge until all six of them admit unintentional murderers as one.

summary: Straight roads were made to the cities of refuge. Two Torah scholars went with the one running there, to talk to the angry relative so he would not hurt him.

chunks.en: And roads were made straight for them from one city to another,
chunks.st: And roads were aligned for them from this city, i.e., all cities, to that city,
chunks.stMore: i.e., they would pave and straighten the access roads to the cities of refuge,

chunks.en: as it says, "Prepare for yourself
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Prepare for you

chunks.en: the road, and divide your land in three."
chunks.st: the road, and divide the borders of your land, which the Lord your God causes you to inherit, into three parts, that every murderer may flee there” (Deuteronomy 19:3).

words.en: and you shall divide in three

chunks.en: And they send two Torah scholars with him,
chunks.st: And the court would provide the unintentional murderers fleeing to a city of refuge with two Torah scholars,

chunks.en: in case the relative of the one who was killed tries to kill him on the way,
chunks.st: due to the concern that perhaps the blood redeemer, i.e., a relative of the murder victim seeking to avenge his death, will seek to kill him in transit,

words.note: The go'el hadam, a relative of the one who was killed.

chunks.en: and they will talk to that relative.
chunks.st: and in that case they, the scholars, will talk to the blood redeemer
chunks.stMore: and dissuade him from killing the unintentional murderer.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.he: אַף הוּא מְדַבֵּר עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ,
chunks.en: He also speaks for himself,
chunks.st: The unintentional murderer also speaks [medabber] on his own behalf
chunks.stMore: to dissuade the blood redeemer,

chunks.en: as it says, "And this is the matter of the killer."
chunks.explain: The word "devar" hints that he speaks for himself.
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And this is the matter [devar] of the murderer, who shall flee there and live” (Deuteronomy 19:4),
chunks.stMore: indicating that the murderer himself speaks.

summary: Anyone who killed would first run to a city of refuge, and Beis Din would bring him back for judgment. One who must go into galus stays there until the Kohen Gadol dies.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:

chunks.en: At first, both one who killed by accident and one who killed on purpose
chunks.st: Initially, either one who killed another unintentionally

chunks.en: hurry to the cities of refuge,
chunks.st: or one who killed another intentionally would hurry and flee to the cities of refuge,

chunks.he: וּבֵית דִּין שׁוֹלְחִין וּמְבִיאִין אוֹתוֹ מִשָּׁם.
chunks.en: and Beis Din sends for him and brings him from there.
chunks.st: and the court in his city would send for him and would bring him from there to stand trial.

chunks.en: One who was found to deserve death in Beis Din,
chunks.st: For one who was found liable to receive the death penalty in court for intentional murder,

chunks.en: they put him to death.
chunks.st: the court would execute him,

chunks.en: One who did not deserve death,
chunks.st: and for one who was not found liable to receive the death penalty, e.g., if they deemed that the death occurred due to circumstances beyond his control,

chunks.en: they let him go.
chunks.st: they would free him.

chunks.en: One who had to go into galus,
chunks.st: For one who was found liable to be exiled,

chunks.en: they bring him back to his place there,
chunks.st: the court would restore him to his place in the city of refuge,

chunks.en: as it says, "And they shall bring him back,
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And the congregation shall judge between the murderer and the blood redeemer…and the congregation shall restore him

chunks.en: the congregation, to his city of refuge."
chunks.st: to his city of refuge,
chunks.stMore: that he fled there” (Numbers 35:24–25), indicating that he had been in a city of refuge before his trial. The Torah states that an unintentional murderer is required to remain in the city of refuge to which he fled until the death of the High Priest. The mishna elaborates: With regard to High Priests, who were appointed in several different manners,

chunks.en: A Kohen Gadol anointed with the special oil,
chunks.st: one anointed with the anointing oil,
chunks.stMore: which was the method through which High Priests were consecrated until the oil was sequestered toward the end of the First Temple period;

chunks.en: or one who wears the extra special clothes,
chunks.explain: The eight special clothes of the Kohen Gadol.
chunks.st: and one consecrated by donning multiple garments,
chunks.stMore: the eight vestments unique to the High Priest, which was the practice during the Second Temple period;

chunks.en: or one who was a Kohen Gadol for a while and stepped down,
chunks.st: and one who received a temporary appointment due to the unfitness of the serving High Priest, who departed from his anointment
chunks.stMore: with the restoration of the serving High Priest to active service,

chunks.en: when they die, the killer goes back home.
chunks.st: their deaths facilitate the return of the murderer
chunks.stMore: from the city of refuge to his home.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: אַף מְשׁוּחַ מִלְחָמָה מַחֲזִיר אֶת הָרוֹצֵחַ.
chunks.en: Even the Kohen anointed for war sends the killer back home.
chunks.st: Even the death of a priest anointed for war to address the soldiers (see Deuteronomy 20:1–7) facilitates the return of the murderer.

chunks.en: So the mothers of the Kohanim Gedolim
chunks.st: The mishna continues: Therefore, the mothers of High Priests

chunks.en: give food and clothing to the people in galus,
chunks.st: would provide those exiled to cities of refuge with sustenance and garments

chunks.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִתְפַּלְּלוּ עַל בְּנֵיהֶם שֶׁיָּמוּתוּ.
chunks.en: so that they will not daven that their sons should die.
chunks.st: so that they would not pray that their sons would die.
chunks.stMore: The more comfortable their lives in the city of refuge, the less urgency they would feel to leave, and the less likely it would be that they would pray for the death of the High Priests.

chunks.en: If after his judgment was decided, the Kohen Gadol died,
chunks.st: If, after the unintentional murderer’s verdict was decided and he was sentenced to exile, the High Priest died,

chunks.en: he does not go into galus.
chunks.st: he is not exiled,
chunks.stMore: as the death of the High Priest exempts him from exile.

chunks.en: If before his judgment was decided,
chunks.st: If it was before his verdict was decided

chunks.he: מֵת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמִנּוּ אַחֵר תַּחְתָּיו,
chunks.en: the Kohen Gadol died and they chose another in his place,
chunks.st: that the High Priest died and they appointed another in his place,

chunks.en: and after that his judgment was decided,
chunks.st: and thereafter his verdict was decided,

chunks.en: he goes home when the second one dies.
chunks.st: he returns from exile with the death of the second High Priest.

summary: In some cases the one in galus can never leave the city of refuge, not even to be a witness or to help the Jewish people. The mishnah also teaches about the area around the city, and what happens if he leaves it.

chunks.en: If his judgment was decided when there was no Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: If the verdict of a murderer was decided at a time when there was no High Priest,

chunks.en: or he killed a Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: and likewise in the cases of one who unintentionally killed a High Priest

chunks.en: or he is a Kohen Gadol who killed,
chunks.st: and in the case of a High Priest who killed unintentionally,

chunks.en: he never leaves there.
chunks.st: the unintentional murderer never leaves the city of refuge.

chunks.en: And he does not leave to be a witness for a mitzvah,
chunks.st: And one who is exiled may not leave the city at all, either for testimony relating to a mitzva,

chunks.en: or to be a witness about money,
chunks.st: or for testimony relating to monetary matters,

chunks.en: or to be a witness in a case of life and death.
chunks.st: or for testimony relating to capital matters.

chunks.en: And even if the Jewish people need him,
chunks.st: And even if the Jewish people require his services,

chunks.en: and even if he is the general of the army of Yisrael
chunks.st: and even if he is the general of the army of Israel

chunks.en: like Yoav ben Tzeruyah,
chunks.st: like Joab ben Zeruiah,

chunks.en: he never leaves there,
chunks.st: he never leaves the city of refuge,

chunks.en: as it says, "where he ran away to."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And the congregation shall restore him to his city of refuge, that he fled there”
chunks.stMore: (Numbers 35:25), from which it is derived:

chunks.en: There he shall live,
chunks.st: There shall be his dwelling,

chunks.en: there he shall pass away,
chunks.st: there shall be his death,

chunks.en: there he shall be buried.
chunks.st: there shall be his burial.
chunks.stMore: The mishna continues:

chunks.en: Just as the city protects him,
chunks.st: Just as an unintentional murderer is admitted to the city of refuge,

chunks.en: so does the area around it protect him.
chunks.st: so is he admitted to its outskirts, located within the Shabbat boundary.
chunks.stMore: Once he entered the outskirts of the city, the blood redeemer may not kill him.

words.note: The area around the city, up to the Shabbos boundary.

chunks.en: If the killer went out past the boundary
chunks.st: In a case where a murderer emerged beyond the Shabbat boundary of the city of refuge

chunks.en: and the go'el hadam found him,
chunks.st: and the blood redeemer found him there,

words.note: The go'el hadam, a relative of the one who was killed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:

chunks.en: it is a mitzvah for the go'el hadam to kill him,
chunks.st: It is a mitzva for the blood redeemer to kill him,

chunks.en: and anyone else is allowed to.
chunks.st: and it is optional for every other person to do so.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: The go'el hadam is allowed to,
chunks.st: It is optional for the blood redeemer,

chunks.en: but anyone else is punished for it.
chunks.st: and every other person is liable for killing him.
chunks.stMore: The previous mishna teaches that the halakhic status of the outskirts of the city is like that of the city itself in terms of the unintentional murderer being provided refuge there. The mishna adds:

chunks.en: A tree that stands inside the boundary
chunks.st: With regard to a tree that stands within the Shabbat boundary of a city of refuge,

chunks.en: with its branches leaning outside the boundary,
chunks.st: whose boughs extend outside the boundary,

chunks.en: or it stands outside the boundary
chunks.st: or a tree that stands outside the boundary

chunks.en: with its branches leaning inside the boundary:
chunks.st: and its boughs extend inside the boundary,

chunks.en: it all follows the branches.
chunks.st: the status of the tree, whether it is considered inside or outside the boundary, in all cases follows the boughs.

chunks.en: If he killed by accident in that same city,
chunks.st: If an unintentional murderer, exiled to a city of refuge, unintentionally killed a person in the same city,

chunks.en: he moves from one neighborhood to another.
chunks.st: he is exiled from that neighborhood where he resided to another neighborhood within that city.

chunks.en: And a Levi who lives there
chunks.st: And a Levite who is a permanent resident of a city of refuge and unintentionally killed a person

chunks.en: moves from one city to another.
chunks.st: is exiled from that city to another city.

summary: The one in galus must tell people why he is there, but he may accept their honor. The Tannaim argue whether he paid rent to the Leviim, and whether he gets back his old job when he goes home.

chunks.en: Similarly,
chunks.st: Similarly,

chunks.en: a killer who went into galus to his city of refuge,
chunks.st: in the case of a murderer who was exiled to a city of refuge

chunks.en: and the people of the city wanted to honor him,
chunks.st: and the people of the city sought to honor him due to his prominence,

chunks.en: he should tell them, "I killed someone."
chunks.st: he shall say to them: I am a murderer.

chunks.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ אַף עַל פִּי כֵן,
chunks.en: If they say to him, "Even so,"
chunks.st: If the residents of the city say to him: We are aware of your status and nevertheless, we wish to honor you,

chunks.en: he may accept it from them,
chunks.st: he may accept the honor from them,

chunks.en: as it says, "And this is the word of the killer."
chunks.explain: He only needs to say it once.
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And this is the matter [devar] of the murderer” (Deuteronomy 19:4),
chunks.stMore: from which it is derived that the murderer is required to say [ledabber] to them that he is a murderer. He is not required to tell them any more than that.

chunks.en: They would pay rent to the Leviim,
chunks.explain: The cities of refuge belonged to the Leviim.
chunks.st: The unintentional murderers would pay a fee to the Levites
chunks.stMore: as rent for their living quarters in the cities of refuge, which were Levite cities;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: They did not pay them rent.
chunks.st: They would not pay a fee to them,
chunks.stMore: but would reside rent free, as they are required to live there by Torah law. They also disagreed with regard to the status of the unintentional murderer when he returns home after the death of the High Priest.

chunks.en: And he goes back to the important job he had before,
chunks.st: He returns to the same public office that he occupied prior to his exile;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: לֹא הָיָה חוֹזֵר לַשְּׂרָרָה שֶׁהָיָה בָהּ:
chunks.en: He does not go back to the important job he had.
chunks.st: He does not return to the office that he occupied.
